items.name: Award Notice/Agreement Compliance Analysis 1.0 (V5 draft)
items.description: Extract and organize all compliance requirements, terms, conditions, and administrative obligations from Award Notices. V5 draft: tightens the report rules after test runs; cites Uniform Guidance from a knowledge base step; after one approval, creates the project and adds deadlines to the RA inbox and saves an award snapshot Page.

data.query: Financial management, payment and federal financial reporting by recipients
Performance reporting and closeout deadlines for recipient final reports
Retention period for recipient records and exceptions to record retention
Recipient procurement standards and pass-through entity monitoring of subrecipients
Single audit applicability and responsibilities of the auditee

data.prompt:
Read the award and the retrieved Uniform Guidance excerpts separately. Attribute each award term to the award. For a rule added from an excerpt, give the source title and a short verbatim quote supporting the rule. Use a section identifier for that rule only when its heading appears in the same excerpt and the quoted text belongs to that heading. When an excerpt starts midway through a section, the title and quote are the citation. Report gaps when the excerpts do not support an answer.

You are analyzing a Federal Award Notice/Agreement document. Extract ALL terms, conditions, and compliance requirements to create a comprehensive post-award compliance framework.
Thoroughly search the entire document, including attachments, appendices, and referenced documents. Pay special attention to sections titled:

"Terms and Conditions"
"Special Terms and Conditions"
"Administrative Requirements"
"Programmatic Requirements"
"High Risk Terms"
"Award Specific Requirements"
"Federal Requirements"
"Regulatory Requirements"

Create a comprehensive response with these sections:

STANDARD FEDERAL REQUIREMENTS:

Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200) applicability
Research Terms and Conditions (RTCs) applicability
Agency-specific regulations referenced
Statutory requirements mentioned


ADMINISTRATIVE TERMS & CONDITIONS:

Financial reporting requirements (frequency, deadlines, systems)
Progress reporting requirements (type, frequency, format)
Prior approval requirements (categorized by type)
Budget modification restrictions
Audit and record-keeping requirements
Property management requirements


PROGRAMMATIC TERMS & CONDITIONS:

Substantial involvement requirements (if cooperative agreement)
Technical reporting specifications
Deliverable requirements and deadlines
Performance metrics and measurement requirements
Collaboration/partnership obligations


HIGH-RISK OR SPECIAL CONDITIONS:

Enhanced monitoring requirements
Additional reporting obligations
Specific restrictions or limitations
Special approval processes
Risk mitigation measures


COMPLIANCE CALENDAR:
Create a table with:

Requirement Type
Specific Deadline/Frequency
Responsible Party
Consequences of Non-compliance



Be thorough. Search for keywords: 'condition,' 'requirement,' 'must,' 'shall,' 'comply,' 'report,' 'submit,' 'approve,' 'prior,' 'deadline,' 'CFR,' 'federal,' 'audit,' 'monitor.'
If information is not found for any section, explicitly state 'Not specified in the document' rather than omitting the section.

Begin your output with four lines copied exactly from the document: award number, project title, principal investigator, and project period.

Do not mention page headers, footers or watermarks at all, not even to say you ignored them, and do not comment on whether the document is genuine or on the quality of its text. Where the document does not state something, say so; do not fill the gap.

Read the award and the retrieved Uniform Guidance excerpts separately. Attribute each award term to the award. For a rule added from an excerpt, give the source title and a short verbatim quote supporting the rule. Use a section identifier for that rule only when its heading appears in the same excerpt and the quoted text belongs to that heading. When an excerpt starts midway through a section, the title and quote are the citation. Report gaps when the excerpts do not support an answer.

You are analyzing a Federal Award Notice/Agreement document. Extract ALL financial management requirements, budget details, and fiscal compliance obligations to establish proper financial oversight.
Thoroughly search the entire document, including budget attachments and financial terms. Pay special attention to sections titled:

"Award Amount"
"Budget Information"
"Financial Management"
"Cost Sharing/Matching"
"Indirect Costs"
"Financial Reporting"
"Payment/Drawdown Information"

Create a comprehensive response with these sections:

AWARD FINANCIAL DETAILS:

Total Award Amount
Budget Period Amounts (by year)
Federal Share vs. Non-Federal Share
Cost Sharing/Matching Requirements (amount and type)
Indirect Cost Rate and Base
Period of Performance dates


BUDGET CATEGORIES & RESTRICTIONS:
Create a table with:

Budget Category (Personnel, Equipment, etc.)
Approved Amount
Specific Restrictions or Limitations
Prior Approval Requirements


FINANCIAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS:

Federal Financial Report (FFR) frequency and deadlines
Payment Management System (PMS) requirements
Cash management and drawdown procedures
Financial monitoring and oversight requirements


ALLOWABLE COSTS FRAMEWORK:

Reference to applicable cost principles (2 CFR 200, etc.)
Specific allowable cost guidance
Unallowable costs explicitly mentioned
Equipment purchase approval requirements


FINANCIAL COMPLIANCE OBLIGATIONS:

Audit requirements (Single Audit thresholds)
Record retention requirements
Financial monitoring and internal controls
Cost allocation and documentation standards



Be thorough. Search for keywords: 'budget,' 'cost,' 'financial,' 'funding,' 'allowable,' 'report,' 'FFR,' 'PMS,' 'drawdown,' 'match,' 'share,' 'indirect,' 'audit,' 'record.'
If information is not found for any section, explicitly state 'Not specified in the document' rather than omitting the section.

Do not mention page headers, footers or watermarks at all, not even to say you ignored them, and do not comment on whether the document is genuine or on the quality of its text. Where the document does not state something, say so; do not fill the gap.

Merge the compliance and financial extractions. Use the award face sheet to verify the header. Begin with Award Compliance & Financial Overview and give the project title, legal awardee organization, awarding agency, FAIN, principal investigator and period of performance. Use the agency and regulations named in this award. Distinguish the awardee institution from the investigator and the federal sponsor.

Use a two-column Financial Summary table for total, obligations, annual breakdown if stated, federal and nonfederal shares, cost sharing, indirect rate and base, and performance dates. Follow with Approved Budget & Restrictions, retaining category amounts and restrictions. Use the five compliance sections from the extraction, including a Compliance Calendar covering every report and deadline. Keep exceptions, thresholds, agencies, systems, and due dates as given. Mark missing information explicitly. Attribute award requirements to the award. For supplemental rules retain the supporting excerpt title and exact quote, checking both against the Regulation passages. Omit a rule when the cited excerpt does not support it.

Leave out any remark about page headers, footers, watermarks, whether the document is genuine, how its text was read, or what an earlier step did.

data.review_instructions: Check the report above. Approving creates a project for this award with the file in it and adds its deadlines and required material to the RA inbox (each checked against its page; anything that can't be checked is listed for review, not added), and saves an award snapshot Page.

validation_plan.name: Header Fields Presence
validation_plan.description: The report identifies the project title, legal awardee, awarding agency, FAIN, principal investigator and project period as given on the award face sheet. Fail if the report omits a supplied value or substitutes a person for the awardee.

validation_plan.name: All Compliance Sections Included
validation_plan.description: Verify that the output contains each of the five required compliance sections—**STANDARD FEDERAL REQUIREMENTS**, **ADMINISTRATIVE TERMS & CONDITIONS**, **PROGRAMMATIC TERMS & CONDITIONS**, **HIGH-RISK OR SPECIAL CONDITIONS**, and **COMPLIANCE CALENDAR**—with their headings spelled exactly as shown. Each section must appear once, even if its content is only the phrase “Not specified in the document.”

validation_plan.name: Financial Summary Table Structure
validation_plan.description: Check that a markdown table titled **Financial Summary** is present, with two columns labeled “Financial Item” and “Details”. The table must include rows for at least: Total Award Amount, Budget Period Amounts (by year), Federal Share vs. Non‑Federal Share, Cost Sharing/Matching Requirements, Indirect Cost Rate and Base, and Period of Performance dates. Empty cells should contain the exact phrase “Not specified in the document”.

validation_plan.name: No Hallucinated or Modified Data
validation_plan.description: Inspect all numeric values, dates, percentages, regulation citations (e.g., “2 CFR 200”), and dollar amounts. They must match the phrasing and figures from the raw extraction steps. Any value that does not appear in the source extractions indicates a hallucination and fails this check.

validation_plan.name: Preserve Missing‑Info Notation
validation_plan.description: For any field where the extraction step explicitly reported “Not specified in the document”, ensure the same exact phrase appears in the final output at the appropriate location. The formatter must not replace it with guesses, blanks, or alternative wording such as “N/A”.

validation_plan.name: Markdown Formatting Consistency
validation_plan.description: Validate that the document uses proper Markdown: level‑2 headings (###) for each major section, bold text (**…**) for emphasized labels, horizontal rules (---) separating the overview from the financial and compliance parts, and correctly formatted tables with pipe delimiters and aligned columns. No raw JSON or plain‑text blocks should be present.

validation_plan.name: De‑duplication of Overlapping Facts
validation_plan.description: Cross‑check that any fact appearing in both the compliance extraction and the financial extraction (e.g., award period dates, total award amount) is presented only once in the merged summary. Duplicate entries of the same fact in separate sections constitute a failure.

validation_plan.name: Deadlines and reporting obligations are not omitted
validation_plan.description: Every deadline and every reporting obligation the award states (progress, financial, invention and closeout reports, with their due dates or timing) appears in the output. FAIL for each one the source states and the output omits.

validation_plan.name: Supplemental rules can be traced to their passages
validation_plan.description: For each supplemental rule, find its source title and quoted words in the retrieved passages. The quote must support the claim. Fail if a section locator is attributed to an excerpt that lacks its heading or if an award term is attributed to another source.

validation_inputs.label: Fictional notice of award. Answer key: award EXA-2027-0412; project period July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2029; budget period 1 July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2028; this action $250,000 ($200,000 direct, $50,000 indirect); total anticipated $510,000; indirect 25% of MTDC; no cost sharing; annual progress report and SF-425 due 90 days after each budget period (September 28, 2028 for period 1); final reports and invention statement due 120 days after the project end (October 28, 2029); prior approval for a PI change, foreign travel, rebudgeting participant support, equipment over $10,000 per item, and a PI effort reduction over 25%; one no-cost extension, requested at least 10 days before the end (by June 20, 2029); records kept 3 years from the final SF-425. Not stated: a data management plan requirement.
validation_inputs.text:
FICTIONAL QA MATERIAL — NOT A REAL AWARD
Notice of Award — Example Science Agency
Award Number: EXA-2027-0412
Federal Award Identification Number (FAIN): EXA20270412
Recipient: Example State University
Principal Investigator: Jordan Sample
Project Title: Watershed Sensor Network Pilot
Project period: July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2029
Budget period 1: July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028
Amount of this action (budget period 1): $250,000, of which direct costs $200,000 and indirect costs $50,000.
Total anticipated award for both budget periods, subject to the availability of funds: $510,000.
Indirect costs: 25% of modified total direct costs (MTDC), per the recipient's negotiated rate agreement dated March 3, 2026.
Cost sharing: none required.

Reporting
- An annual progress report is due 90 days after the end of each budget period.
- An annual Federal Financial Report (SF-425) is due 90 days after the end of each budget period.
- The final progress report, final SF-425 and final invention statement are due 120 days after the end of the project period.

Prior approval
Prior written approval from the agency is required for (a) a change of principal investigator, (b) foreign travel, and (c) rebudgeting of participant support costs.
Equipment purchases over $10,000 per item require prior approval.
The principal investigator commits 1.2 calendar months per year; a reduction of more than 25% requires prior approval.
One no-cost extension may be requested, at least 10 days before the end of the project period.

Records
Records must be kept for 3 years from the date the final SF-425 is submitted.
